subject: zoology
question_text: What are claspers? Which group of fishes possesses them?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.55, VSAQ 113). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK WORDING: the book writes that claspers are 'formed near pelvic fins'. They are formed FROM the pelvic fins — the inner edges of the pelvic fins are modified into the claspers — and the card says so.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What they are
steps.margin_note: Say what they are, where they come from and what they do. Three short lines.
lines: Claspers are the copulatory organs of a male
They are formed from the modified inner edges
They carry sperm into the cloaca of the female,
steps.why: A clasper is a fin turned into a copulatory organ, so naming the fin it comes from explains both its position and its use.
common_mistakes: Writing that claspers are found in the female. They are a male character.
Placing claspers on the pectoral fins. They are modified pelvic fins.
steps.memory_tip: Pelvic fin plus male equals clasper: the fin becomes the organ.

steps.label: The group
steps.margin_note: Name the group and one example. The second mark is for the group, not for more detail.
lines: Claspers are found in the males of
They are absent in the males of bony fishes.
steps.why: Claspers go with internal fertilisation, and internal fertilisation is the cartilaginous pattern, so the group follows from the organ.
common_mistakes: Naming bony fishes. Claspers are absent in the males of bony fishes.
Giving no example. One named fish makes the group answer complete.
steps.memory_tip: Internal fertilisation needs a clasper, and only cartilaginous fishes fertilise inside.

insider_note: The question has two halves and each is worth one mark, so an answer that describes claspers beautifully but never names cartilaginous fishes loses half.
